newsitem.title: MEXICO: TMM denies having track rights problem.
newsitem.headline: TMM denies having track rights problem.

text.p: Mexican firm Transportacion Maritima Mexicana said on Tuesday its unit Texas-Mexican Railroad (Tex-Mex) had been authorised to move traffic to and from Mexico on track of Union Pacific/Southern Pacific.

Responding to a news report that it might not have permission to use the track, TMM said Tex-Mex, which it jointly owns with Kansas City Southern Industries Inc, had received authorisation from the U.S. Surface Transportation Board following an application in March.

"As was announced at the time, and as a function of the authorisation for the Union Pacific/Southern Pacific merger, the Board granted these rights to Tex-Mex to move traffic from and to Mexico," TMM said.
The Board approved the Union Pacific/Southern Pacific merger in July.

TMM and Kansas City Southern Industries Inc, through a partnership called Transportacion Ferroviaria Mexicana, won 50-year operating rights to Mexico's Northwest Railway last week with a bid of 11.07 billion pesos ($1.4 billion), almost three times higher than competing bids.
